llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: The Odyn helper exposes signing, attestation, KMS, app-wallet, and S3 helper methods, but these are documented Nova platform capabilities and are not secretly invoked by the skill.
[SDI-2] expected: S3 put/delete helpers are present in the app template, but S3 is documented as feature-gated by Nova advanced settings; no hidden destructive storage action was found.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The GitHub PAT remote-url guidance is risky because it can expose or persist the token, but it is user-visible setup guidance rather than artifact-backed exfiltration or deception.
[SQP-2] expected: KMS derivation and storage mutation APIs are disclosed in SKILL.md and the Odyn reference; they are sensitive but coherent with the skill's TEE app-development purpose.
[VirusTotal] expected: The clean VirusTotal telemetry is consistent with local artifact review, but it was treated only as supporting signal.
llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to build and deploy Nova apps. Use a fine-grained GitHub token limited to the target repo, avoid embedding tokens in remote URLs when possible, rotate any token exposed in shell history or Git config, review generated code before deployment, and narrow egress settings for production apps.
llm.summary: This is a disclosed Nova app build/deploy helper, but users should handle the GitHub and Nova credentials carefully.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: nova-app-builder
Version: 2.3.1

The nova-app-builder skill bundle is a legitimate developer tool designed to scaffold, build, and deploy Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) applications on the Sparsity Nova platform (sparsity.cloud). The bundle includes a project template, a deployment script (scripts/nova_deploy.py), and comprehensive documentation (SKILL.md and references/). While the skill requires sensitive inputs such as a Nova API key and a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT), these are used strictly for their stated purposes—communicating with the Nova Platform API and pushing code to the user's repository. The code logic is transparent, lacks obfuscation, and contains no evidence of data exfiltration, backdoors, or malicious prompt injection.
